title: Loop currents in Haldane's model and in time-reversal-breaking superconductors
abstract: We present a theoretical study of optical manifestations of loop currents in Haldane's model and in time-reversal-breaking superconductors. For Haldane's model, we calculate the expectation value of loop currents in terms of model parameters and relate it with the integrated optical spectral weight for the frequency-dependent ac Hall conductivity. Thus, experimental measurements of the latter can provide information about the presence and magnitude of steady loop currents in the system. Then we elaborate on loop currents in a chiral superconductor on the honeycomb lattice, studied earlier by Brydon et al. (2019). We demonstrate that a sharp optical absorption peak in the ac Hall conductivity originates from excitations between the lower and upper Dirac bands, activated by the time-reversal-breaking superconductivity. The frequency of the peak is twice the energy difference between the Fermi level and the Dirac point. The optical spectral weight of the peak is directly related to the magnitude of loop currents induced in the unit cells by the chiral superconducting pairing, in similarity to Haldane's model.
summary: This theoretical work examines how loop currents manifest optically in topological materials, specifically Haldane's model and chiral superconductors. By relating the loop current expectation value to the frequency-dependent ac Hall conductivity, the authors predict sharp absorption peaks whose spectral weight directly quantifies the underlying chiral currents. This offers a pathway for experimental detection of topological superconductivity.
main_problem: The study investigates the optical manifestations of loop currents in topological systems, specifically Haldane's model and time-reversal-breaking superconductors.
main_result: The authors establish a direct relationship between the optical spectral weight of the ac Hall conductivity and the magnitude of the induced loop currents in both models.
method: Theoretical calculations involving Green's functions, Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonians, and the analysis of optical conductivity ($\sigma_H(\omega)$) via Kubo-like formulas.
model_or_system: The models analyzed are Haldane's model (a Chern insulator on the honeycomb lattice) and a chiral superconductor on the honeycomb lattice, both described using lattice Hamiltonians and BdG formalism.
key_observables: Loop currents ($\langle \hat{I}_{	ext{lc}} angle$), frequency-dependent ac Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}(\omega)$), and the optical Hall spectral weight ($	ext{W}_{	ext{Hall}}$).
important_parameters: The superconducting gap ($\Delta$), Fermi level ($\mu$), and the energy difference between Dirac bands ($\omega_{	ext{peak}}$).
main_assumptions: Approximations are made regarding the superconducting gap relative to the Fermi energy ($\Delta \ll 2\mu$), and the analysis focuses on the optical response rather than the DC response.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Haldane's model on the honeycomb lattice, the spatial distribution of loop currents, and the energy eigenvalues near the K point showing optical transition peaks.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first calculating loop currents in Haldane's model, then extending the methodology to analyze the ac Hall conductivity in chiral superconductors, deriving relations between the spectral weight and loop currents.
why_interesting: The connection drawn between topological currents (loop currents) and measurable optical responses ($\sigma_H(\omega)$) provides a powerful, experimentally verifiable diagnostic tool for characterizing exotic superconducting and topological phases.
